tour.overview:
Bali is the only island of Indonesia where the majority of people follow Balinese Hinduism, a faith woven into every part of daily life: offerings of flowers and rice placed each morning, temples in every village and family compound, and ceremonies all year round. Ubud, in the green hills of the interior, has been the island's centre of art, dance and craft since painters from Europe settled here in the 1930s. Bali's rice terraces and their thousand-year-old subak water system, governed by water temples, have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2012.

This private day explores the culture of Ubud with a licensed Balinese guide and a car. You visit a family compound, walk through the Tegallalang rice terraces, take part in a purification ritual at Tirta Empul, have lunch with a view of the jungle, meet the monkeys of the Sacred Monkey Forest and end at Ubud Palace and the market.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Bali
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; steps in the rice terraces and at Tirta Empul

WHAT YOU SEE
• A Balinese family compound.
• The Tegallalang rice terraces.
• Tirta Empul water temple.
• The Sacred Monkey Forest.
• Ubud Palace and Ubud market.

WHY THIS WORKS
We reach Tegallalang and Tirta Empul early, before the heat and the crowds, and leave the town of Ubud for the afternoon.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Bali, families, photographers and anyone curious about Balinese culture.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want sunsets and sea temples, choose our Tanah Lot and Uluwatu tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
A sarong and sash are required in temples; they are provided. Women who are menstruating are asked by Balinese custom not to enter temples. Traffic in Bali is slow: from the south coast, allow about 1 hour 30 minutes each way.

days.name: A Balinese family compound, Tegallalang rice terraces, Tirta Empul, lunch, the Sacred Monkey Forest and Ubud Palace
days.description:
What to expect: the culture, faith and landscapes of Ubud in one day, with a licensed Balinese guide, private car, entrance fees and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:30. North of Ubud, you visit a traditional family compound, a walled home where several generations live in separate pavilions around a courtyard, with a family temple in the most sacred corner, facing the holy mountain Agung. Your guide explains the Balinese calendar, the daily offerings called canang sari and the ceremonies that mark each stage of life.

At Tegallalang, you walk down into the rice terraces that step down a valley shaded by coconut palms. Your guide explains the subak, the cooperative system that shares water between farmers through canals and tunnels, managed by priests of the water temples since the 9th century, and the cycle of planting and harvest, with the goddess Dewi Sri watched over in little shrines in the fields.

At Tirta Empul, a temple founded in 962 around a spring that never runs dry, Balinese come to bathe in the holy water. Wearing a sarong, you can join the ritual, moving along the row of stone spouts in the purification pool, praying and splashing your head at each one, guided by your Balinese guide. After lunch on a terrace overlooking the jungle, with Balinese dishes such as babi guling, nasi campur and satay lilit, you visit the Sacred Monkey Forest in Ubud, where some 1,200 long-tailed macaques live among banyan trees, moss-covered statues and three temples. You end at Ubud Palace, home of the royal family, whose courtyards and carved gates are used for evening dance performances, and the art market opposite. You are back at your hotel at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:45 – Balinese family compound.
09:30 – Tegallalang rice terraces.
11:00 – Tirta Empul and purification ritual.
12:30 – Lunch with a jungle view.
14:00 – Sacred Monkey Forest.
15:00 – Ubud Palace and art market.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A Legong or Kecak dance performance at Ubud Palace in the evening can be added.
• A coffee plantation visit can be added; we do not visit places that keep caged civets for kopi luwak.
• Keep sunglasses, hats and food away from the monkeys.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, entrance fees, sarong and offerings, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: dance performance, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we join the purification ritual?
faq.answer: Yes, respectfully, wearing a sarong, with your guide's explanation of the prayers. You get wet, so bring a change of clothes.

faq.question: Are the entrance fees included?
faq.answer: Yes: Tegallalang, Tirta Empul and the Sacred Monkey Forest, plus the sarong and offerings.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, with a jungle view. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: How long is the drive from the south coast?
faq.answer: About 1 hour 30 minutes each way from Seminyak, Kuta or Nusa Dua, depending on traffic.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the monkeys and the rice fields. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The rice terraces and Tirta Empul have steps and slopes; the Monkey Forest has paved paths.

faq.question: Are the monkeys dangerous?
faq.answer: They are wild and can grab things. Keep food out of sight, don't touch them and follow your guide's advice.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops at silver, batik or coffee shops unless you ask.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Bali but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes covering shoulders, comfortable shoes, a change of clothes for the ritual, and sun protection.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October is the dry season. From November to March it rains most afternoons, but the rice fields are lush.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
